newsitem.title: UK: Freight rates steady on Handy and Panamax demand.
newsitem.headline: Freight rates steady on Handy and Panamax demand.

text.p: Holidays in Taiwan and S.Korea were partly responsible for a dull ending to the week although the BFI gained 4 points today to 998 with route 2 US Gulf/Japan heavy grain marked up from $19.03 to $19.25.

Strong Handy-sizes demand on the Continent was evident and there was a healthy turnover in Panamaxes in the east. But otherwise owners continued to face difficulties with 1980-built 60,000 dwt Koyo-type Panamax open prompt E.Med said to be able to obtain little more than the equivalent of $3,000 daily for transatlantic business, against running costs of about $5,000 daily.

An over-age 15,000 dwt tweendecker prompt W.Africa was able to obtain the equivalent of only $4,000 daily basis delivery Brazil for Atlantic business. Clearly owners will be unable to sustain such losses indefinitely and widespread talk of tonnage laying-up is a strong feature of the current freight market.

GRAIN - Cargill failed to confirm or deny details of their fixture of 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for Oct 18/25, but grain brokers were confident the rate agreed was either a basically unchanged level of $18.90 or $19.00.
Cargill also declined to confirm their early Oct fixture of 60,000 heavy grain U.S.Gulf/Continent widely believed to be also an unchanged $8.00.

Dreyfus were rumoured to have booked a Panamax on timecharter with barley from the Continent to Saudi Arabia and fixed a similar size on voyage basis from US gulf to S.Korea and China, but details were lacking.
Fresh panamax grain business today included Cargill 50/52,000 barley Continent/Saudi Arabia for Oct 5/11 and Seatrans 50,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Egyptian Med for Oct 5/15 (ideas $9.00).
Continental remained open for an early Oct Panamax for Nopac/Japan, a position which has appeared to become tighter this week.

Glencore were busy in the Handy-size trades from the Continent where rates were also strengthening, although an exception was the 1974-built Virginia which was booked for 25,000/10 barley Antwerp and Spanish Med/China at close to a weak $35.00.
Glencore have fixed 25,000/10 barley Cardiff/Saudi arabia at about $25.00 and are rumoured to have bid tonnage for a similar quantity Rouen/Cuba at well in excess of the last fixed level of S19.00.
Romac have fixed 17,600 wheat Immingham/Tunisia and Andre are said to have covered a 25,000 grain stem from Rouen to Libya, but further details are lacking.

New handy-size grain orders included Cargill 25/27,500 wheat N.France/Algeria for Oct 2/7, Copenship 25,000 wheat Immingham/Trieste and/or Venice for Oct 5/10, and Toepfer 30,000 wheat St Lawrence to Poland for Oct 15/22. In the east Pisces Pioneer 35,000 was fixed on private terms for grain from Nopac to S.Korea.
MINERALS - The caper market remains in the doldrums in all areas and little activity was seen in this category today.

But Panamax fixtures were quite numerous in the North Pacific where some rates edged upwards. Darya Preeth 73,200 dwt was believed to have been fixed by Aimcor from the US West Coast to the Continent with petcoke on private terms.
There was still no confirmation of rumoured coal fixtures of Torm Tekla 69,268 dwt (by Cobelfret) and Galene 73,670 dwt (by Yukong) from Richards Bay to Morocco and Continent respectively.

HANDY-SIZES - SCM were understood to have paid a hefty rate for a Canadian Forest relet from Rostock to the Lakes, following Brodin's expensive fixture yesterday of 1976-built Alpha 28,193 dwt delivery Gibraltar prompt trip via the Baltic for a Lakes round at $7,500 daily. Kavo Maleas 25,739 dwt is rumoured fixed from the Continent to the Med at a firm rate on private terms. But Von Appen fixed Hua Tu 31,217 dwt from the Continent to the far east at a modest $8,050 daily. Little was reported elsewhere but Olympic Miracle 29,000 was booked by Pan Ocean delivery prompt Djakarta for an Australian round at $6,900 daily. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7771
